problems.stem: The AI's teaching advice on your published dialogue page reads smoothly and sounds confident, and the page renders fine. Is the advice itself ready to publish?
options: Yes; fluent, confident advice is accurate advice.
No; fluent advice must still be checked claim by claim against evidence before it is published.
Yes, as long as the page loads.
No, because advice can never appear on a public page.
problems.explanation: Fluency is a style property, not an evidence check; each claim in the advice has to be verified before it goes on the public page.

problems.stem: Your dialogue page shows the teacher persona block at the top. What role does that persona actually play in the artifact?
options: It is flavor text that makes the chat sound friendlier.
It is a constraint that fixes the AI's role, audience, and limits, so the dialogue can be checked against it.
It is decoration a reviewer is expected to skip.
It only matters if the page also has custom styling.
problems.explanation: The persona is the contract the dialogue must honor; treating it as decoration means the tone, audience, and bounds were never really set.

problems.stem: While drafting your page with a current assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or Gemini), it suggests opening with 'Research shows students remember 90% of what they teach others (Dale, 1969).' It sounds authoritative. What is the strongest move?
options: Accept it; a citation means the claim is verified.
Reject it and log the rejection, because the statistic is fabricated and the cited author never made the claim.
Accept it but remove the citation so no one can check it.
Keep it because it makes the page look researched.
problems.explanation: Confident, fluent advice with a citation still has to pass claim-by-claim verification; this is the fabricated statistic and misattribution debunked in 04.03, so you reject it and record the rejection in your trace.

problems.stem: After pushing your dialogue page to GitHub Pages, what confirms the artifact is actually done?
options: The AI's first draft is pasted whole, so the work is complete.
Opening the live URL and seeing the labeled dialogue plus your trace of accepted, modified, and rejected suggestions.
The AI said it looked good.
problems.explanation: One unedited draft is not a revision; the artifact is done when the live page carries the dialogue and the accept/modify/reject trace a reviewer can audit.
